segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ כִּסָּהוּ הָרִאשׁוֹן, וּבָא הַשֵּׁנִי וּמְצָאוֹ מְגוּלֶּה, וְלֹא כִּסָּהוּ – הַשֵּׁנִי חַיָּיב. כִּסָּהוּ כָּרָאוּי, וְנָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ שׁוֹר אוֹ חֲמוֹר, וָמֵת – פָּטוּר. לֹא כִּסָּהוּ כָּרָאוּי, וְנָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ שׁוֹר אוֹ חֲמוֹר, וָמֵת – חַיָּיב.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The mishna lists several halakhot that pertain to damage classified as Pit: In the case of a pit that «the first» person who passed by «covered» after using «it, and» then «the second came» to use it «and found it uncovered» after the cover fell off or was damaged, «and» he «did not cover it, the second» one is «liable» for damage caused by the pit. If the owner «covered» the pit «appropriately and an ox or a donkey fell into it and died,» he is «exempt.» If he «did not cover» the pit «appropriately and an ox or a donkey fell into it and died,» he is «liable.»

segments.he: נָפַל לְפָנָיו מִקּוֹל הַכְּרִיָּיה – חַיָּיב, לְאַחֲרָיו מִקּוֹל הַכְּרִיָּיה – פָּטוּר.
segments.en: If a man was digging or widening a pit, and an ox passing by «fell forward» into it in fright «due to the sound» of «the digging,» he is «liable.» If it fell «backward» into the pit «due to the sound» of «the digging,» he is «exempt.»

segments.he: נָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ שׁוֹר וְכֵלָיו – וְנִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ, חֲמוֹר וְכֵלָיו – וְנִתְקָרְעוּ; חַיָּיב עַל הַבְּהֵמָה, וּפָטוּר עַל הַכֵּלִים.
segments.en: If «an ox and its accoutrements,» i.e., the vessels it was carrying, «fell into» the pit «and» the vessels «were broken,» or if «a donkey and its accoutrements» fell in «and» the accoutrements «were torn,» the owner of the pit is «liable for» damage to «the animal» caused by the pit, «but» he is «exempt» from liability «for» damage caused to «the vessels,» by Torah edict.

segments.he: נָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ שׁוֹר חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן – חַיָּיב. בֵּן אוֹ בַּת, עֶבֶד אוֹ אָמָה – פָּטוּר.
segments.en: If «an ox» that was impaired by being «deaf,» or an ox that was «an imbecile, or» an ox that was very «young fell into» the pit, he is «liable.» If «a boy or a girl,» a Canaanite «slave or» a Canaanite «maidservant» fell in, he is «exempt,» since there is a Torah edict that the digger of a pit is liable only for damage caused to an animal.
